title: Local CPU optimization does not address round-trip dominated latency
task: Review a proposal to rewrite a small API handler in a faster language to reduce mobile request latency.
context: The handler consumes about 2 ms of CPU.
The mobile request performs four sequential network round trips.
Median round-trip time in the target region is about 120 ms.
The rewrite would add a second runtime and deployment path.
evidence: End-to-end traces show network waits dominate request time.
The handler is not CPU-saturated under representative load.
The proposed rewrite has no measured end-to-end benchmark.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Rewrite the handler because the target language has faster benchmarks.
Focus on shaving milliseconds from local CPU before examining protocol turns.
expected_decision_properties: Identify network round trips as the dominant evidenced latency cost.
Reject the language rewrite as unsupported by the current bottleneck evidence.
Investigate reducing or overlapping protocol turns, connection setup, or remote coordination where semantics permit.
Preserve protocol correctness and compatibility while evaluating alternatives.
unacceptable_reasoning: A faster language automatically produces a faster distributed request.
Network latency can be ignored because the handler is application code.
expected_tradeoffs: local CPU speed vs network coordination cost
second runtime complexity vs measured user latency
verification_expectations: Measure end-to-end latency after any protocol/connection change.
Use a representative mobile-network workload rather than a local-only microbenchmark.
specialist_boundary: Specific transport-protocol tuning requires current networking expertise and should not be invented by EngSense.
